item.title: Davis High Theater Presents: The Tragedy of Macbeth — Sat Oct 24, 7:00 PM — Richard Brunelle Performance Hall
item.description: If you knew you were destined for power, would you let fate take its course or would you grab destiny by the wheel and hit the gas? When three mysterious witches awaken Macbeth’s hunger for power, ambition sets in motion a bloody chain of betrayal, murder, and madness. Shakespeare’s iconic, haunting tragedy explores the dangerous consequences of mistaking destiny for something we can control. Location Brunelle Theater @ 315 W 14th Street. Performances Friday, October 16, Saturday October 17, Friday October 23, Saturday October 24 @7:00PM Sunday October 18 and Sunday October 25 @2:00PM Tickets $15 general admission, $10 for DJUSD students, and $5 on Sundays for DJUSD students. item.title: Rock of Ages — Sat Oct 24, 7:30 PM — Woodland Opera House
item.description: It’s 1987 on Los Angeles’ legendary Sunset Strip, where the Bourbon Room is the heart of the rock-and-roll scene. When aspiring musician Drew meets small-town newcomer Sherrie, their dreams of love and stardom collide with a developer determined to transform the Strip. With the Bourbon Room fighting for survival and a legendary rock star headed to town, this hilarious, high-energy jukebox musical celebrates big dreams, true love, and the unforgettable spirit of ’80s rock, all set to classic hits from Whitesnake, Styx, Pat Benatar, Twisted Sister, and more. It’s part rock concert, part comedy, part love letter to the ’80s…and completely ready to rock your socks off!!! item.title: Yolo Basin Foundation Docent Training — Sun Oct 25, 9:00 AM
item.description: Event Date: October 24 – 25, 2026 Yolo Basin Foundation invites you to engage with your community by learning how to lead tours of the Yolo Bypass Wildlife Area and the City of Davis Wetlands. Volunteers who become wetland tour docents lead guided visits through these unique natural areas, welcoming wildlife enthusiasts, families, students, and retired members of our community. Tours of the Yolo Bypass Wildlife Area take place October through June on the third Sunday of the month, from 9:00 a.m. to noon. Tours of the City of Davis Wetlands are offered the first Sunday of the month, from 9:00 a.m. to 11:00 a.m., throughout the year. item.title: Birds & Bikes — Sun Oct 25, 12:00 PM — Axis Gallery
item.description: Axis Gallery is proud to announce Birds & Bikes, a collaborative art exhibition bringing together regional artists to explore the poetic intersections of avian flight and human motion. Running from October 2 through November 1, 2026, the exhibition showcases a dynamic range of works from intricate metal sculptures and imaginative textile art to curated gallery shop goods, celebrating the beauty of migration alongside the engineering of daily travel. The exhibition features a direct partnership with the City of Sacramento Office of Arts and Culture (OAC) Art in Public Places program and North Natomas Jibe. Birds & Bikes serves as an artistic tie-in to the upcoming Birds and Benches project, which will install artist-designed public benches across North Natomas Regional Park. Visitors are invited to experience the unique ecology and transit identity of the Natomas Basin through a collaborative lens, discover one-of-a-kind art pieces, and browse handcrafted items in the East Gallery Pop

item.description: Art in Action: Lovely Landscapes Sunday, October 25, 1-3 PM $5 Members, $10 Non-Members (per person, all materials included) Create the landscape of your dreams! Inspired by Danilo Campos’ exhibit, draw and paint your very own landscape on canvas and craft a decorative frame for your painting with cardstock, gold paint, and ribbon. How it works: Art in Action engages kids in art projects that are fun, creative, and collaborative with their family members. This is a drop-in program for ages 5-12. item.title: October Open Mic & Music Trivia Halloween Themed — Sun Oct 25, 6:00 PM — The Melon Ball – Watermelon Music
item.description: This month’s theme for Open Mic & Music Trivia is Halloween. Come in costume, sing songs about Halloween or anything else ghoulish spooky, or witchy. Of course, if you don’t want to play-a-long and just do your own thing, you are still welcome! Whether you’re looking for a venue to share your own talents or just looking to enjoy hearing (and seeing) some local performers, we invite you to this free monthly event. We provide the sound, stage and lights – the rest is up to you. Play us your favorite song, tell us some jokes, act out a scene from your favorite play with friends. We will continue to feature our Music Trivia contest throughout the evening in between acts. The winner will receive a $20 Watermelon Music gift card! item.title: Healing Arts One-Time Workshop — Mon Oct 26, 10:00 AM — Pence Gallery
item.description:
Healing Arts One-Time Workshop Monday, October 26, 10-11:45 AM $5 Members, $10 Non-Members (all materials included) Part of the Pence’s Healing Arts Program and run by facilitator Amy Vidra, this one-time workshop focuses more broadly on themes related to depression, anxiety, or major life changes. Through the process of art making, participants will have opportunities for discussion, education, and connecting with peers in a safe and supportive space. Registration is required in advance through our website, and space is limited to the first 8 participants who register. Participants must be 18 or older, and no art experience is necessary. This program is generously sponsored by Bob & Joanne Andresen. Register here (REQUIRED): https://pencegallery.org/education/programs/workshops-and-classes/ If you register for this session and are unable to attend, please let us know in advance. Any questions? Email pencegallery@gmail.com.

Every second Friday, stroll downtown Davis to discover fresh exhibits, opening receptions, live music, hands-on activities, and direct chats with local and regional artists at 10+ galleries, co-ops, and businesses. Support our vibrant arts scene, uncover unique talent and styles, and soak up the lively energy – ideal for friends, families, dates, or solo adventures. item.title: International Festival Davis — Sat Nov 7, 2:00 PM — International House Davis
item.description: Join us on November 7 at International House Davis for I-Fest 2026, our International Festival Davis! For one day, we open our doors wide to celebrate and uplift the many cultures and people who make our region so vibrant. Explore cultural and artisan booths throughout I-House, enjoy food trucks out front, and experience a full lineup of performances on our backyard stage. It’s an open house in the truest sense: for the day, this is your house too, and every culture and community has a place here. I-Fest is a celebration, but your participation also supports the work I-House does all year long: welcoming newcomers, supporting English learners, and helping people from around the world find connection and community in Davis. At a time when many of us are feeling anxious or disconnected, creating spaces for joy, belonging, and connection feels more important than ever. item.title: Un-Coding AI in the Classroom: 2-Day Workshop for Faculty and Instructors — Thu Dec 10 — DataLab Classroom
item.description:
Generative AI is reshaping the landscape of higher education, raising important questions for teaching, learning, and academic integrity. Designed for faculty and instructors across all disciplines and requiring no prior technical background, this two-day workshop unpacks genAI and offers practical strategies for the university classroom. Whether you are curious about how these models work, eager to integrate AI into your teaching, or cautious about its impact on student learning, this series offers a supportive, nuanced space to explore. Participants will gain a clear foundational understanding of large language models (LLMs), evaluate the opportunities and limitations of genAI, and engage in hands-on practice configuring customized and privacy-protected AI learning environments for their courses.
The workshop runs Thursday-Friday December 10-11 from 9 AM - 4 PM daily with a break for lunch. Full participation in both days is recommended as topics build across sessions.

item.description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering Update 8/14/25: **We're still active**, but we primarily use Discord to chat and plan events. (See group description for invite link.)
We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.
People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.
Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.
